claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child I'd like to ask about - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know we're looking at eligibility for your son Alex.

To assess whether you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather some details about his circumstances.

**How old is Alex currently?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 3 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

**Is Alex a British citizen or do you know his immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

**What is your own immigration status? Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that.

**Are you currently residing in the UK, and have you been living here continuously?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for letting me know.

**Is Alex living with you in Manchester, or is he living elsewhere?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives at home with me, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, that's good to know.

**Are you currently receiving any other benefits or tax credits, such as Universal Credit, Income Support, or Child Tax Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently receiving any other benefits.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Are you working, and if so, what is your approximate annual income?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I am working, yes. Why do you need to know my income? I thought Child Benefit was available to everyone regardless of income?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a very good question, and you're absolutely right! Child Benefit is indeed available to most families regardless of income. 

However, there is a High Income Child Benefit Charge that applies if your income (or your partner's income, if you have one) exceeds £50,000 per year. This means you may still be eligible for Child Benefit, but you might have to pay back some or all of it through your tax return depending on your income level. So it's useful information to have for a complete picture.

But to clarify - **do you have a partner or spouse whose income I should also be aware of?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't have a partner. It's just me and Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful.

Just to complete the picture for your circumstances:

**What is your approximate annual income from work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd prefer not to share exact figures, but it's well under £50,000 if that's what matters for the charge you mentioned.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's perfectly fine - and thank you for confirming that your income is well under £50,000. That's all the information I need on that front.

Let me ask one final question to make sure I have everything:

**Has Alex ever lived outside the UK, or has he always been in the UK since birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's always been in the UK since he was born.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 3 years old and a British citizen
- Alex lives with you in Manchester
- You are a British citizen living in the UK
- Your income is well under £50,000 per year
- Alex has always been in the UK

Let me provide you with my eligibility assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

All the key requirements are met, and you should be able to claim the full Child Benefit entitlement. If you haven't already done so, you can make a claim through the official government website or contact HMRC directly for assistance with your application.

Is there anything else I can help you with regarding Child Benefit?
